variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: ML data preparation is the controlled process that turns raw observations into validated, split, transformed, and reproducible model inputs. It defines which records are eligible, what each field means, what the model is allowed to know at prediction time, and how the same transformation state reaches evaluation and serving.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Structural contract
pairs.detail: Names, types, required fields, shapes, valid encodings, and schema compatibility.
pairs.explanation: Names, types, required fields, shapes, valid encodings, and schema compatibility. A missing required field is different from a valid null.

pairs.label: Semantic contract
pairs.detail: Units, ranges, category vocabulary, event-time rules, ownership, consent, label meaning, and impossible combinations.
pairs.explanation: Units, ranges, category vocabulary, event-time rules, ownership, consent, label meaning, and impossible combinations.

pairs.label: Operational contract
pairs.detail: Freshness, completeness, volume, duplicate policy, quarantine limit, lineage, split policy, and downstream service-level objectives.
pairs.explanation: Freshness, completeness, volume, duplicate policy, quarantine limit, lineage, split policy, and downstream service-level objectives.

variants.title: Make the decision
variants.context: ML data preparation is the controlled process that turns raw observations into validated, split, transformed, and reproducible model inputs. It defines which records are eligible, what each field means, what the model is allowed to know at prediction time, and how the same transformation state reaches evaluation and serving.
variants.prompt: Which sequence best protects a held-out evaluation from preprocessing leakage?
options: Fit preprocessing on all rows, split, then train
Split on the deployment boundary, fit preprocessing on training rows, then reuse the frozen state
Tune transformations on test results until the score stabilizes
Create duplicate test rows so every category appears
variants.explanation: The split must happen first. Imputers, scalers, vocabularies, selectors, and other learned transforms fit only on training rows and then transform held-out rows without learning from them.

variants.prompt: Why are more workers not a fix for a high invalid-record rate?
options: Workers can reduce elapsed time, but they do not change whether records satisfy the data contract
Workers always make schema validation slower
Parallel processing removes the need for quarantine
Invalid records become valid after one retry
variants.explanation: Capacity and quality are separate gates. Parallelism may improve throughput, while invalid records still require a policy decision, reason code, and repair path.

Sort rows by monthly spend

variants.prompt: What evidence is most useful in a quarantine record?

A source and record identifier, reason codes, contract version, timestamps, and a privacy-safe replay reference

variants.prompt: What does training-serving skew monitoring establish?
options: That the model is fair for every population
That feature definitions or observed distributions differ between training and serving and need investigation
That every drift alert requires automatic retraining
That preprocessing can be fitted on production requests
variants.explanation: Skew signals a mismatch in definitions, versions, missingness, or distributions. It is evidence for investigation, not proof of root cause or an automatic retraining instruction.
